title: Input inequality rejects paired codes
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, and let $C,n,s$ be natural numbers such that $C$ is at least the number of states plus $6$ times the number of work tapes plus $5$. If distinct Boolean strings $x,y$ both have length $n$, and $c,d$ are configurations on these inputs, then the CNF formula enforcing equality of the two inputs evaluates to false on the assignment given by the bits of the concatenated configuration codes, with any out-of-range variable assigned false.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is at least the number of states plus $6$ times the number of work tapes plus $5
